subject: health
unitTitle: Staying Safe at Home, Outside, and Online
title: Correction and reflection: device and online safety basics
essentialQuestion: How do I spot a hazard early and choose the safest next step?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online.
People online are not always who they say they are.
Anything sent can be saved and shared onwards, even if it seems to disappear.
If something online is scary, mean, or asks you to keep a secret, tell a trusted adult right away.
Telling is always the right thing to do, and it is the adult's job to help.
privacySafeScenario: All required evidence uses fictional or public situations. The learner never has to disclose personal health, body, treatment, feelings, family, sexual, or substance-use information.
studentTask: Write two facts. Use the lesson idea about device and online safety basics. Choose one safe next step. Name an adult or help source.
knowledgeCheck: Name the fact. Fix the wrong claim. Choose a safe action. Name who can help.
completionCriteria: I explain device and online safety basics.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.
adaptationChoices: Show one short direction at a time. Allow reading aloud, word cards, typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking. Help may repeat a direction but may not choose the fact, action, reason, or help source.
extensionChallenge: Create a new fictional or public case about device and online safety basics. Include enough facts, choices or constraints, and support authority for another learner to reason safely. Add an accurate explanation of acceptable variation; use no real person's private information.
accessibilitySupports: Show one action at a time.
Offer a vocabulary card and extra time.
Accept typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking for equal credit.
trustedAdultNote: If a real situation feels unsafe or raises a health concern, pause the lesson and tell a parent, guardian, teacher, school staff member, or another trusted adult. A qualified health professional gives medical advice. In an emergency, get an adult and use the local emergency service.

optionalReflection.prompt: Optional and private: Make up one example that helps you remember device and online safety basics. Keep it for yourself. You do not need to show it or prove that you completed it.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, body comparison, or appearance scoring.
This task never requires calorie counting, dieting, or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires sharing medical history, a diagnosis, treatment, medication, feelings, family conflict, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires advice about an individual learner's treatment, medication, food, supplement, or exercise plan.
standards: Michigan Health Practice 4: Decision Making and Problem Solving
Michigan Health Practice 3: Information and Resource Seeking
Michigan Health Topic (Grades 3-5): Safety and Injury Prevention
learningGoal: I can explain device and online safety basics, use facts, choose a safe next step, and name who can help.

lessonExperience.learnerTitle: Learn and apply: device and online safety basics
lessonExperience.privacyNotice: Write only about the made-up people. Keep private information private.

entryCheck.heading: Start with a fact
entryCheck.directions: Choose the sentence that states a fact.
choices: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online.
This one detail proves everything about a person's health.
A popular statement about device and online safety basics needs no evidence.
entryCheck.support: A fact is stated in the lesson or supported by reliable evidence. An assumption adds a conclusion the information cannot establish.
entryCheck.treatment: This entry check is unscored. Use the support or prerequisite route before continuing when needed.

explanation.heading: Understand device and online safety basics
paragraphs: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online.

explanation.importantDistinction: Learning about device and online safety basics supports accurate reasoning and safe next steps; it does not authorize a diagnosis, individualized treatment advice, a person label, or a value judgment.
explanation.decisionRule: FIND the smallest gap. USE a different model. CORRECT one step. RETRY on a fresh case.

vocabulary.heading: Words for device and online safety basics

terms.meaning: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online.
terms.boundary: This idea does not diagnose, label, or determine the value of a person.

terms.meaning: facts or reliable evidence that can change the interpretation, choice, or next step
terms.boundary: A guess, popularity, or a personal judgment is not relevant evidence by itself.

terms.meaning: the responsible adult, qualified professional, service, or public authority able to help with the situation
terms.boundary: Naming a support route does not make the learner responsible for diagnosis, treatment, or emergency management.

vocabularyCheck.heading: Check the words
vocabularyCheck.selfCheck: A complete check uses the meaning of device and online safety basics, one accurate fact, and the responsible support route without labeling a person.

canonicalPracticeContext.heading: Use the authored practice situation
canonicalPracticeContext.situation: Someone in a game chat tells Sam they are also nine, asks which school Sam goes to, and asks Sam to keep it a secret from Sam's parents. What is wrong here, and what should Sam do?
canonicalPracticeContext.treatment: This canonical context may support teaching or discussion. It does not replace the separate fresh independent, mastery, or remediation-retry cases.

modelExample.heading: Watch the reasoning: device and online safety basics
modelExample.situation: A fictional Northside response about device and online safety basics only repeats the topic name and adds a guess about a person. The approved fact is: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online. The response must be corrected with a different organizer before a new case is attempted.
relevantFacts: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online.
People online are not always who they say they are.
modelExample.assumptionOrDistraction: A popular or confident statement about device and online safety basics is not automatically accurate and cannot establish a person's health, motives, or character.
possibleActions: Name the exact gap, use the alternate organizer, correct a parallel case, and retry fresh.
Replace the evidence task with a private reflection.
modelExample.successCheck: The model uses the lesson fact, explains the connection, stays within the learner role, and names responsible help when it is needed.
workedReasoning: Locate one observable gap: fact, vocabulary, reasoning, process order, or support route.
Use a contrast or visual organizer instead of repeating the first explanation.
Correct one parallel example, then remove the cue before a fresh retry.

guidedReasoning.heading: Try a different case with support
guidedReasoning.situation: A fictional Riverside youth group must explain or act on device and online safety basics. The group has this reliable lesson information: People online are not always who they say they are. It has not been given any person's private health information.
availableChoices: Use the stated facts and compare safe options.
Pause and contact the responsible help source.
turnOne: Name an adult who can help.
guidedReasoning.cue: Look for the situation, safe choices, relevant information, and who can help.
feedbackMoves: If a response adds a guess, replace it with a fact from the case or lesson.
If device and online safety basics is named without explanation, link one fact to the concept or process.
If a choice is reasonable but the reason is missing, add the fact that supports it.
If a response seeks disclosure, diagnoses, shames, or exceeds the learner role, switch to the fictional facts and the approved help route.
Accept an equivalent typed, handwritten, drawn-and-labeled, signed, selected, or spoken response when it shows the same reasoning.
guidedReasoning.turnTwo: Fix one sentence. Use a fact and a safe next step.
guidedReasoning.releaseCondition: Continue when the response uses a stated fact, applies device and online safety basics, and gives a safe next step without private disclosure or a person label.

independentEvidence.heading: Show what you know on a fresh case
independentEvidence.situation: A fictional Maple Community Center response about device and online safety basics contains a fact error, an unsupported conclusion, and no help route. The approved fact is: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online. Identify and repair each gap before the separate fresh retry.
directions: Use the lesson idea about device and online safety basics.
Name an adult or help source.
permittedSupports: read-aloud or one direction at a time
typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking
independentEvidence.independenceBoundary: Support may restate a direction or provide access. It may not choose the controlling fact, conclusion, action, reason, safety judgment, or help route.
successCriteria: I explain device and online safety basics.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.

freshMasteryCheck.heading: Check the idea in a new place
freshMasteryCheck.situation: A fictional Lakeside school committee reviews device and online safety basics. The committee knows: Anything sent can be saved and shared onwards, even if it seems to disappear. It must correct one unsupported claim and choose a safe next step.
freshMasteryCheck.freshnessNote: This case is different from the model, guided case, and independent case. Do not copy their conclusions.

remediation.heading: Try a different model
remediation.trigger: Use this route after an observable gap in a fact, vocabulary meaning, reasoning step, process order, or help route for device and online safety basics.
remediation.prerequisite: First restate this approved fact in your own words: Personal information — full name, address, school, phone number, passwords — stays private online.
remediation.alternateExplanation: Use a four-box decision map: SITUATION, SAFE CHOICES, RELEVANT INFORMATION, and HELP. Fill each box with case facts before writing a conclusion.
contrast: Sufficient: uses a stated fact about device and online safety basics, explains the connection, and stays within the learner role.
Needs revision: repeats a topic word, adds a guess, or gives an action with no factual reason or responsible help source.
remediation.guidedCorrection: Cross out the guess. Circle the fact. Add one safe action.

freshRetry.situation: A fictional Oak Street library receives a new question about device and online safety basics. Staff provide this approved fact: People online are not always who they say they are. The learner must respond without using the Northside, Riverside, Maple, or Lakeside conclusions.

remediation.exitCriterion: Return to the independent route when the learner accurately uses a fact, applies device and online safety basics, explains a safe response, and identifies support without answer-bearing help.
remediation.nextRoute: If the same gap remains, return to the named prerequisite with an adult instructor; do not replace the task with private reflection.

laterTransfer.timing: Use in a later lesson or a separate session.
laterTransfer.prompt: Apply device and online safety basics to a meaningfully different fictional or public case. Retrieve the concept, use relevant facts, justify a safe response, and identify the responsible support or authority route.
laterTransfer.masteryBoundary: The current independent response is one evidence occasion. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence now and accurate later retrieval or transfer.

contentProvenance.objective: Teach and consolidate device and online safety basics, correct any errors from the unit, explain the corrections, and identify where the unit transfers.
